notes: Interactive, adapted to stdin: interactor.py sends the official 8869-word dictionary (the statement's attachment) and T, then per game the first letter and g / s / - marks per guess; it scores as grader.cpp does (its total on the sample grader's answers equals grader.cpp's, 100025) and accepts at an average of 98, as the statement's full 100 sits at the best play. The statement sample's seven games (panic, apple x4, above, cobra) are too few to average, so for T < 1000 it instead requires every game solved within five guesses; orig.cpp solves all seven (average 92.9). 4261154 and 4261160 passed by restricting candidates to the sample grader's srand(0) answers, so on other uniform answers they average 11.8 and are no reference; their files are gone and these records stay. 4261087 and 4261177 are grader-only (word.h, no main); under the same stdin main they average 95.5 and 96.1 on seed 1 (partial credit), below the bar. orig.cpp is a corpus-written reference: per guess it picks the dictionary word minimising a greedy expected-guesses cost over the remaining candidates, memoised by game history; it averages 99.6 to 100.5 on seeds 1 to 7 and --max, about 5 s per case.
